issues.body: The self-test described as proving every row declares label|kind|probe|pattern only rejects NF<4. A row such as `|command|tool|pattern` or `label|command|tool|` has four fields and passes that assertion; an empty label is then silently skipped by `_selftest_env_blocked`. The current two rows are valid and are additionally covered by dependency-specific assertions, so this does not undermine the present change, but a later added requirement could be accidentally omitted fail-open if its label is empty.
issues.fix_hint: Validate every parsed row's label, kind, probe, and pattern as non-empty (and preferably reject unsupported kinds) rather than checking only NF<4; add a fixture showing that an empty-label requirement is rejected rather than skipped.
issues.title: Requirement-row validation permits an empty label or pattern

verdict.summary: The dependency preflight is fail-closed, runs before changed-path classification, and refuses the registry gate whenever either declared runtime dependency is absent. The implementation correctly separates the refusal decision from best-effort consumer reporting, safely treats unknown probe kinds as absent, and tests present/absent behavior, real probes, real-tree consumer matching, and gate wiring. I found no blocker or major issue. One minor extensibility gap remains in the requirement-table shape assertion.
